deep.reconstruction:
This page has no computations. It is a programmatic table of contents (a 'Disposition'), marked '=1 Bl.' and foliated 133, for a treatise headed 'Theorie eines Systems gleichverzweigter algebraischer Functionen und von Integralen solcher Functionen'. Its items line up closely, in content and order, with the sections of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). That paper's Part I treats Riemann surfaces, the Dirichlet principle and Abelian integrals. Part II, sections 5 ff., treats gleichverzweigte algebraische Functionen, classes and moduli. The page is therefore an early plan of that paper. Item by item, in modern terms:

(1) The character (behaviour) of these functions, i.e. meromorphic functions on a fixed n-sheeted branched covering T of the z-sphere.

(2) Vanishing or becoming infinite of first order at a point of the surface T, with local parameter (z-a)^(1/k) at a branch point. Hence the character of their singularities.

(3) Determination of such functions by their branching type (the surface) and their singularities via the Dirichlet principle. This is the existence theorem for harmonic/analytic functions with prescribed singularities on T.

(4) The simplest substitutions they undergo. My reading: on crossing the cuts the integrals change linearly with constant coefficients, i.e. by additive constants (periods). The words read 'und dreien Constanten' are uncertain.

(5)-(6) These items are deleted. They concerned algebraic functions and the dependence of the singularities.

(7) Reduction to the problem of determining the simplest branching types, and of determining the algebraic functions belonging to them.

(8) Every derivative of an algebraic function s(z) is rational in s and z. If F(s,z)=0 then ds/dz = -F_z/F_s, a rational function of s and z [explicit formula supplied by me].

(9) Everywhere-finite integrals: integrals of the first kind, p linearly independent.

(10) μ-times-infinite algebraic functions: functions with μ simple poles. The 1857 paper's count is μ - p + 1 arbitrary constants for general poles, the Riemann inequality. A further line concerns other functions in the same system, roughly 'Gibt ... in einem Systeme'.

(11) Determining all equally-branched algebraic functions belonging to the same class as a given equation. This is birational equivalence: the field of rational functions of s and z.

(12) The problem (or number) of the moduli of a class: in the 1857 paper, 3p-3 for p>1.

(13) The equations of each class of lowest degree: normal forms of minimal degree.

A marginal note defines 'Klassen von Gleichungen' as those transformable into each other by rational substitutions, corresponding to a class of equally-branched algebraic functions. The previous page, on counting branch points from coinciding roots (w + 2v = 2(n-1)m), belongs to the same preparatory material.
errors: No mathematical derivations appear on the page, so there are no computational errors to report. The outline itself is consistent with the published 1857 paper.

results.what: Plan: existence of functions on a branched covering surface with prescribed branching and singularities via the Dirichlet principle
results.modern_name: Existence theorem for meromorphic functions / Dirichlet principle on Riemann surfaces

results.what: Derivative of an algebraic function expressed rationally in s and z
results.modern_name: Implicit differentiation; the function field C(s,z) is closed under d/dz
Abelian differentials of the first kind (holomorphic 1-forms), dimension p

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft outline of the published 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857), all of whose contents are well known and credited to Riemann. Its interest is purely genetic: it shows the planned order of topics and the deleted items. It contains no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: ds/dz = -F_z/F_s is rational in s and z (item 8)
The moduli count 3p-3 for p>1 vanishes only at p=1, where the count is special (1 modulus) (item 12)
Riemann–Hurwitz for an n-sheeted cover of the sphere with w simple branch points: p = w/2 - n + 1. Example: hyperelliptic with 6 branch points gives p = 2

transcription_corrections: Item 12 probably reads 'Anzahl der Moduln einer Klasse' rather than 'Aufgabe der Moduln', matching section 12 of the 1857 paper.
Item 10 'Mayer ...' is likely 'μ mal' or 'Allgemein μ mal unendliche algebraische Functionen' (μ-times-infinite functions).
Item 4 may read 'linear mit constanten Coefficienten und additiven Constanten' rather than 'und dreien Constanten'.
Item 2 refers to 'einen Punkt der Fläche T' (Riemann's standard surface T), not T'.
The heading 'I' before 'Theorie' and the marginal sign at item 12 are editorial marks, not part of the text.
